sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: setlist.fm: a search for an artist's setlists (setlist.fm/search?artist=…, with or without a tour, country, city or venue) gets the same "Setlists" button as an artist's page: every setlist of the search as one table, named after the search's choices ("setlist.fm search: Bruce Springsteen · Land of Hope & Dreams American Tour").

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: setlist.fm links: a link to setlist.fm's search for an artist's setlists — every Tour cell of the setlist.fm tables links one — now has its card and window like the other setlist.fm links, also without an API key: they are read from setlist.fm's search page itself. The window lists the search's setlists with their set times, 10 at a time ("Load 10 more"), with the tours and venues on the left.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: setlist.fm tables: the page now scrolls sideways, so a table wider than the window can be read to its last column. setlist.fm's own stylesheet turns sideways scrolling off for the whole page.
setlist.fm tables: a show at a stage inside a venue ("NAC Opera Hall at National Arts Centre, Ottawa") no longer repeats the venue in the Event column.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: setlist.fm: on the list of a venue's setlists (setlist.fm/venue/…) or an artist's (setlist.fm/setlists/…), a new "Setlists" button lists every setlist as one filterable, sortable table: date (linked to the setlist), artist or venue, event, tour, doors, start and end (24-hour), how many songs the list shows ("12+" when there are more) and those songs. The rows come from setlist.fm's own pages, 10 setlists each, one page after another; no API key is needed. Upcoming shows stay out of the table. With your setlist.fm API key set, the table's setlist links get their card and window on setlist.fm too. Its own switch, ⚙️ Settings → 🎤 setlist.fm → "Enable on setlist.fm", is on by default.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: setlist.fm windows (link preview, with your setlist.fm API key): set times. The Setlists table of a venue, an artist or a tour has a "Set times" column (doors, and the show from start to end), and a setlist's window lists Doors, Scheduled, Start (how long after doors) and End (how long the show was). The times are on a 24-hour clock, as on MusicBrainz. setlist.fm's API has no set times, so they are read from setlist.fm's own pages: only once the window is open, never for the hover card, two pages for every 20 setlists, at most one a second. "…" means the page is still being read, "?" that it could not be (⟳ Try again), "—" that setlist.fm has none.

setlist.fm window of a venue: what the API leaves out, read from the venue's own page with the set times: its address, when it opened (or was open), other names, its web links and how many attendances setlist.fm's users have logged.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: setlist.fm window of a venue or an artist (link preview, with your setlist.fm API key): the dates in the Setlists table no longer break onto a second line ("2026-10-20" wrapped at its hyphens).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: setlist.fm window of a venue or an artist: "In the loaded setlists" lists the artists and tours (a venue's) or the tours and venues (an artist's) as small tables you can sort and filter, most setlists first. The number of setlists is a button: it keeps the Setlists table on the right to that artist, tour or venue, and works together with the table's text filter. A second click, or the ✕ of the "Only …" label above the table, shows them all again.

setlist.fm windows: a tour is a link, as on setlist.fm. It goes to setlist.fm's search for that artist and tour; in the window it opens the tour's setlists (20 at a time, "Load 20 more", its venues on the left), and ← Back returns. A setlist's window links its tour the same way.
